text:
Iris (Events): Hey finance - I paid the deposit for our conference booth with my personal AmEx because the corporate card was still pending. Vendor sent an invoice for $12,500 but my card posted $12,875 (includes a 3% card processing fee). Can we reimburse the full posted amount? Also vendor invoice lists 'booth rental' but our sponsorship cost center needs 'marketing-sponsorship' line item.
expense-bot: Reminder: Attach vendor invoice, proof of payment (card statement), and manager approval for sponsorship spend.
Iris (Events): attaching: vendor invoice PDF (no processing fee line), my bank posting screenshot $12,875, and the confirmation email from the vendor showing deposit accepted.
Elaine (Finance): Thanks Iris. Two issues: 1) We generally reimburse the invoiced amount. Processing fees charged by a vendor to a personal card are reimbursable only if the fee is unavoidable and pre-approved. 2) We need to code the charge to Marketing-Sponsorship. Please get manager approval for the processing fee exception.
Carlos (Sponsorship): I approve the sponsorship cost coding to marketing-sponsorship. Regarding the 3% fee - did the vendor state they would charge for card payments?
Iris (Events): vendor confirmation doesn't call out the processing fee. They said "standard processing applied by payment processor" in a follow-up message when I asked. I didn't think to insist on ACH. I can ask them for an adjusted invoice showing $12,500 and the $375 processing fee separately.
Megan (Legal): Also check the exhibitor agreement: if the invoice needs to show "sponsorship" language for accounting, we should get an amended invoice. I'll review the contract quickly.
Elaine (Finance): Action items: 1) Iris - request an amended invoice from the vendor that breaks out booth rental ($12,500) and processing fee ($375). If vendor refuses, provide a written vendor attestation. 2) Iris - upload proof of payment (card posting) and manager approval for the fee. 3) Megan - if contract allows, ask vendor to reissue invoice with "Marketing - Sponsorship" line or we will code internally but keep attestation for audit.
Iris (Events): pinged vendor. They replied: "We can issue a credit memo for $375 but cannot reissue with new description. We can email a breakdown." Uploaded their email.
Carlos (Sponsorship): I can sign off on the processing fee as a one-time exception given short lead time. Adding approval note in expense form.
Elaine (Finance): OK we have: vendor email offering credit memo, card posting proof, and manager approval for fee. For audit record we'll accept the vendor email + internal approval. Please change expense category to "Sponsorship - Events" so it maps to marketing spend.
Iris (Events): changed category and added Carlos's approval note. Also uploaded the vendor email that acknowledges the $375 processing fee and the offered credit memo.
expense-bot: Expense created: "Conference booth deposit - TechSummit" status: awaiting payment. Link: https://expenses.internal/reports/EXP-3199
Elaine (Finance): Good. We'll reimburse you $12,875 as "personal card reimbursement" and then process the vendor credit memo when it arrives (we will offset the $375 against future vendor payments). Coding: MARKETING-SPONSOR. Expect payment in 3-7 business days. Case #FIN-2026-158.
Megan (Legal): Filing a quick note: vendor credit memos should be captured and matched in AP. If vendor doesn't issue a credit within 30 days, escalate to procurement.
Iris (Events): Thanks everyone - appreciate the quick help. I'll follow up on the credit memo and close out the ticket. :pray:
